summary: iterquarry 2.1.3 executes an encrypted module blob via a concealed unpinned dependency
details: iterquarry 2.1.3 ships quarry.libseal, a 335-byte encrypted blob with magic header LSL1, and executes it as a Python module through the external libseal package. The advertised pairwise() entry point in recipes.py imports load_sealed_sync, seal_sync, read_module from libseal, calls load_sealed_sync(file=SEALED, module_path="quarry", password="pairwise") to decrypt the shipped blob, loads it as a module, and invokes.buffer() on it. The pairwise function is re-exported from the top-level package, so any caller using the documented API triggers the decrypt-and-execute path on opaque author-controlled bytes that are not reviewable from source. pyproject.toml declares dependencies = ["libseal"] unpinned, while the README states that version 2.1.3 has no third-party dependencies — the dependency required to decrypt and execute the shipped blob is concealed from readers. Because libseal is unpinned, whichever version of that PyPI package is installed at the time of resolution controls what the encrypted blob actually does; future libseal releases silently change the executor behind the opaque payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
